To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of the EpoR in breast tumors is significantly higher in the epithelial fraction of breast tumors than in the endothelial fraction, and that EpoR levels in the epithelium of breast tumors are significantly higher than in normal mammary tissue.
the expression of the erythropoietic receptor (EPOR) was higher in epithelial cells than endothelial cells of primary breast tumors, and the level of EPOR was correlated with that of VEGF.

the use of the erythropoietic agent darbepoetin alfa does not appear to be associated with an increased risk of thromboembolic events, although the possibility of an increased risk of arterial thromboembolic and cerebrovascular events cannot be ruled out.
the use of erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) in cancer patients should be restricted to those with anemia caused by the disease and not to those with chemotherapy-induced anemia.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our data support the notion of a role for Epo in the pathogenesis of human breast cancer, and that this role is mediated through Epo receptor (EpOR).
we have developed an assay for quantifying erythropoietic receptor (Epo-R) in the epithelial and endothelial fractions of fresh breast tumors.

we have shown a significant difference in the expression of EPO and EPO-R between the epithelial and endothelial fractions of breast tumors, and that this difference was not due to differences in the expression of these proteins between the epithelial fractions of primary tumors and normal breast tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the epithelial cells of breast tumors have significantly higher erythropoietic receptor levels than their endothelial cells, and these differences are even greater in triple-negative tumors.
there is a significant difference in the levels of EpoR expression between the epithelial and endothelial fractions of the same primary breast tumor.
the EPO receptor is expressed in breast cancer cells and is associated with a worse outcome.
